- `netcheck` is installed in `/root` (the exec working directory, also on `PATH`) and refreshed with its
  member list on every `bin/jump` run, which `bin/setup` makes, as it does for the nodes.
- The VPC router has no route for a connector's own address, so instances cannot reach nodes directly.
  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.
 - `netcheck` is installed in `/root` (the exec working directory, also on `PATH`) and refreshed with its
  member list on every `bin/jump` run, which `bin/setup` makes, as it does for the nodes.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.
e- `netcheck` is installed in `/root` (the exec working directory, also on `PATH`) and refreshed with its
  member list on every `bin/jump` run, which `bin/setup` makes, as it does for the nodes.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

- The VPC router has no route for a connector's own address, so instances cannot reach nodes directly.
  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.
e- `netcheck` is installed in `/root` (the exec working directory, also on `PATH`) and refreshed with its
  member list on every `bin/jump` run, which `bin/setup` makes, as it does for the nodes.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.
,- `netcheck` is installed in `/root` (the exec working directory, also on `PATH`) and refreshed with its
  member list on every `bin/jump` run, which `bin/setup` makes, as it does for the nodes.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.
e- `netcheck` is installed in `/root` (the exec working directory, also on `PATH`) and refreshed with its
  member list on every `bin/jump` run, which `bin/setup` makes, as it does for the nodes.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.
h- `netcheck` is installed in `/root` (the exec working directory, also on `PATH`) and refreshed with its
  member list on every `bin/jump` run, which `bin/setup` makes, as it does for the nodes.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.
t- `netcheck` is installed in `/root` (the exec working directory, also on `PATH`) and refreshed with its
  member list on every `bin/jump` run, which `bin/setup` makes, as it does for the nodes.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.
 - `netcheck` is installed in `/root` (the exec working directory, also on `PATH`) and refreshed with its
  member list on every `bin/jump` run, which `bin/setup` makes, as it does for the nodes.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.
`- `netcheck` is installed in `/root` (the exec working directory, also on `PATH`) and refreshed with its
  member list on every `bin/jump` run, which `bin/setup` makes, as it does for the nodes.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.
r- `netcheck` is installed in `/root` (the exec working directory, also on `PATH`) and refreshed with its
  member list on every `bin/jump` run, which `bin/setup` makes, as it does for the nodes.

  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  member list on every `bin/jump` run, which `bin/setup` makes, as it does for the nodes.
- The VPC router has no route for a connector's own address, so instances cannot reach nodes directly.
  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.
 - `netcheck` is installed in `/root` (the exec working directory, also on `PATH`) and refreshed with its
  member list on every `bin/jump` run, which `bin/setup` makes, as it does for the nodes.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.
r- `netcheck` is installed in `/root` (the exec working directory, also on `PATH`) and refreshed with its
  member list on every `bin/jump` run, which `bin/setup` makes, as it does for the nodes.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.
n- `netcheck` is installed in `/root` (the exec working directory, also on `PATH`) and refreshed with its
  member list on every `bin/jump` run, which `bin/setup` makes, as it does for the nodes.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.
 - `netcheck` is installed in `/root` (the exec working directory, also on `PATH`) and refreshed with its
  member list on every `bin/jump` run, which `bin/setup` makes, as it does for the nodes.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.
o- `netcheck` is installed in `/root` (the exec working directory, also on `PATH`) and refreshed with its
  member list on every `bin/jump` run, which `bin/setup` makes, as it does for the nodes.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.
`- `netcheck` is installed in `/root` (the exec working directory, also on `PATH`) and refreshed with its
  member list on every `bin/jump` run, which `bin/setup` makes, as it does for the nodes.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.
 - `netcheck` is installed in `/root` (the exec working directory, also on `PATH`) and refreshed with its
  member list on every `bin/jump` run, which `bin/setup` makes, as it does for the nodes.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

- The VPC router has no route for a connector's own address, so instances cannot reach nodes directly.
  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.
d- `netcheck` is installed in `/root` (the exec working directory, also on `PATH`) and refreshed with its
  member list on every `bin/jump` run, which `bin/setup` makes, as it does for the nodes.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

- The VPC router has no route for a connector's own address, so instances cannot reach nodes directly.
  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.
i- `netcheck` is installed in `/root` (the exec working directory, also on `PATH`) and refreshed with its
  member list on every `bin/jump` run, which `bin/setup` makes, as it does for the nodes.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.
a- `netcheck` is installed in `/root` (the exec working directory, also on `PATH`) and refreshed with its
  member list on every `bin/jump` run, which `bin/setup` makes, as it does for the nodes.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.
n- `netcheck` is installed in `/root` (the exec working directory, also on `PATH`) and refreshed with its
  member list on every `bin/jump` run, which `bin/setup` makes, as it does for the nodes.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.
s- `netcheck` is installed in `/root` (the exec working directory, also on `PATH`) and refreshed with its
  member list on every `bin/jump` run, which `bin/setup` makes, as it does for the nodes.

- The VPC router has no route for a connector's own address, so instances cannot reach nodes directly.
  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.
,- `netcheck` is installed in `/root` (the exec working directory, also on `PATH`) and refreshed with its
  member list on every `bin/jump` run, which `bin/setup` makes, as it does for the nodes.

  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.
p- `netcheck` is installed in `/root` (the exec working directory, also on `PATH`) and refreshed with its
  member list on every `bin/jump` run, which `bin/setup` makes, as it does for the nodes.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  member list on every `bin/jump` run, which `bin/setup` makes, as it does for the nodes.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.
a- `netcheck` is installed in `/root` (the exec working directory, also on `PATH`) and refreshed with its
  member list on every `bin/jump` run, which `bin/setup` makes, as it does for the nodes.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.
 - `netcheck` is installed in `/root` (the exec working directory, also on `PATH`) and refreshed with its
  member list on every `bin/jump` run, which `bin/setup` makes, as it does for the nodes.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.
d- `netcheck` is installed in `/root` (the exec working directory, also on `PATH`) and refreshed with its
  member list on every `bin/jump` run, which `bin/setup` makes, as it does for the nodes.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.
 - `netcheck` is installed in `/root` (the exec working directory, also on `PATH`) and refreshed with its
  member list on every `bin/jump` run, which `bin/setup` makes, as it does for the nodes.

  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.
c- `netcheck` is installed in `/root` (the exec working directory, also on `PATH`) and refreshed with its
  member list on every `bin/jump` run, which `bin/setup` makes, as it does for the nodes.

  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.
r- `netcheck` is installed in `/root` (the exec working directory, also on `PATH`) and refreshed with its
  member list on every `bin/jump` run, which `bin/setup` makes, as it does for the nodes.

  member list on every `bin/jump` run, which `bin/setup` makes, as it does for the nodes.
- The VPC router has no route for a connector's own address, so instances cannot reach nodes directly.
  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.
_- `netcheck` is installed in `/root` (the exec working directory, also on `PATH`) and refreshed with its
  member list on every `bin/jump` run, which `bin/setup` makes, as it does for the nodes.

  `bin/gwmap` (run by `bin/setup` and `bin/jump`) gives each node an alias address in the gateway's /96
  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  and DNATs it to the node on the gateway, so from the jump `ping -6 fd20:0:32::1:0:101` reaches a node.
  The map is in `state/<fleet>/gw-aliases` and is what netcheck uses here. It lives on the running gateway
  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.
P- `netcheck` is installed in `/root` (the exec working directory, also on `PATH`) and refreshed with its
  member list on every `bin/jump` run, which `bin/setup` makes, as it does for the nodes.

  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.

  only, so a gateway restart loses it until the next `bin/setup` or `bin/gwmap`. Aliases are numbered by
  sorted node name, so a resize renumbers them.
